editorialNarrative.hook: Toyota brings endurance momentum, Chevrolet a technical reset. Kostecki's Ford crew must also adapt to a late engineer change before the Mountain.
editorialNarrative.synopsis: Race 30 starts at 11:30am Sydney time on Sunday 11 October at Mount Panorama: 161 laps of the 6.213km circuit, roughly 1000 kilometres. It closes the Ryco Enduro Cup before the championship Finals. The Bend tested reliability over 500km; Bathurst doubles that demand and adds the consequence of every handover and pit call. Supercars' forecast, updated on 6 October, raises the possibility of Saturday and Sunday showers, not a confirmed wet race. Changing conditions would make tyre calls another pressure point for crews already balancing endurance and outright speed.
editorialNarrative.formCopy: Chaz Mostert and Fabian Coulthard won at The Bend, with Ryan Wood and Jaxon Evans also reaching the podium. All five Toyotas finished that first endurance test, giving the new manufacturer evidence beyond short-race speed. Chevrolet arrives with a separate change: Supercars has approved reduced roll-cage centre-of-gravity ballast for the Camaro from Bathurst, with no corresponding Mustang or Supra adjustment. That changes the technical backdrop, not a guaranteed finishing order.
editorialNarrative.closingCopy: Brodie Kostecki and Todd Hazelwood will race without George Commins, the engineer behind Kostecki's 2024 Bathurst win. A mountain-biking injury has ruled Commins out; DJR team manager Tom Moore takes over. Moore already knows Kostecki from their years in the same teams, so this is not a partnership built from scratch. For Ford supporters, the new tension is whether a proven contender can keep its familiar rhythm with a different voice on the radio. Toyota's first Great Race campaign and Chevrolet's revised ballast add rival ambitions, not a guarantee that any badge has the answer.
